idiom_name: parent-owned state published on the framework's implicit channel, plus namespaced children
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: the parent creates the state (value plus update callbacks), publishes it on the framework's implicit channel — an ambient context, a scope object handed to child-render callbacks, a projection query that finds declared children, or a group object children add themselves to — and renders the children inside that scope. Children declare participation (their value, order or identity) and read the published state; they never receive it as a prop from the call site and never mutate it directly, only through the published callbacks. Export the family as one namespaced symbol and make misuse loud: a child used outside its parent must fail with a clear diagnostic, because no type system can express the parent-child membership constraint. The two canonical React implementations are (a) Context API (FlyOutContext.Provider + useContext in children) and (b) React.Children.map + cloneElement (which passes props directly to children without a separate channel). Context API is preferred because it works through intermediate wrapper components, while cloneElement breaks when children are wrapped.
code_sketch:
family := create_family(owner)
    state := { value, set_value }          # one owner for the family
    publish(state)                         # implicit channel: context / scope / group
    render(children)                       # children read the published state

child := declare_identity(value) [
    s := use_published()                   # implicit, never a prop from the call site
    s.set_value(value) on activate         # mutate only through the parent
]

# call site: <Family><Family.Item a/><Family.Item b/></Family>
pitfalls: Publishing through a module-level singleton instead of a per-instance channel: every instance of the widget on the page then shares one selection.
Letting children mutate the state directly (rather than through published callbacks) makes the parent's invariants unenforceable and untestable.
Without an explicit fail-fast check, a misplaced child renders nothing or reads a stale default value instead of reporting the misuse.
The channel is invisible at the call site, so the hidden parent-child contract must be documented and tested as a contract, not left to code reading.
Clone-style injection (React.cloneElement) silently overwrites props the child already received from its own caller, including event handlers — causing invisible callback conflicts.
Creating a new context value on every render (without memoization) forces all consuming children to re-render on every parent render, even when the actual state has not changed.
Mixing unrelated state into one context value (a 'god context') causes unnecessary re-renders for every piece of state change, even in children that only care about one slice.

Wrapping children in an intermediate component (e.g. `
`) breaks the channel when using cloneElement, because the intermediate div is not the parent — use Context API or forward the context explicitly to fix.

Failing to provide a meaningful default context value (or a guard/throw in the hook) produces cryptic null-reference errors when a child is used outside the parent, instead of a clear developer-facing diagnostic.

Wrong move: ship the family as a published library API relying only on the implicit channel -> failure: no type system (PropTypes, Flow, TypeScript) can express 'this child requires that parent', so misuse surfaces at runtime for every consumer -> instead: keep the implicit channel for parts shipped and versioned together, and prefer explicit props or a typed items API where misuse must be caught by the compiler.

Wrong move: leave channel-injected props in the child's public props interface -> failure: editors suggest consumers pass them and the parent's injection silently overwrites whatever was supplied -> instead: keep injected state out of the child's props type entirely and read it only from the published channel, so the call site cannot set values it does not own.

Wrong move: model children as JSX components when they are pure data with no independent behaviour -> failure: the composition still cannot be type-checked and readers must decode indirection to see what renders -> instead: pass a typed data array (items/sections) and render the parts internally, reserving the compound form for genuinely open composition.
